CMS INDUSLAW advised Freehand on this fundraise. The transaction team consisted of Winnie Shekhar (Partner), Shantanu Singh (Partner) and Ravishankar M (Senior Associate). Forcibly de-boarding passenger from bus is a consumer case, not human rights violation: Madras HC
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently held that a passenger’s complaint that he was forcibly de-boarded from a government bus and denied a ticket amounted to a consumer grievance and cannot ordinarily be treated as a human rights violation [ Chidambara Selvan v. TNHRC ]. A Bench of Justices M Dhandapani and N Dilip Kumar , therefore, set aside a Tamil Nadu State Human Rights Commission (SHRC) order directing the payment of compensation to a passenger who alleged that a bus conductor had behaved rudely with him before forcing him to de-board a bus. Justice M Dhandapani and Justice N Dilip Kumar The Court was hearing a petition filed by S Chidambara Selvan, an employee of the Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation. He challenged an SHRC order passed in September 2019, by which a sum of ₹30,000 was ordered to be paid to bus passenger on account of his human rights being violated by the crew of the bus. The dispute arose from an incident on January 16, 2016. items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta asks CJI Surya Kant to replace Rajasthan HC Acting Chief Justice for misusing office
items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta has asked Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant to appoint a Chief Justice from another State to head the Rajasthan High Court "with immediate effect". In letters dated August 2, August 10 and August 17 accessed by Bar & Bench , Justice Mehta has accused acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma of manipulating case listings in favour of rich litigants and misusing his administrative powers ahead of his retirement, due later next month. Justice Sharma was appointed as Rajasthan High Court judge in November 2016 and transferred to the Patna High Court in 2022. When he sought repatriation on health grounds, the Collegium headed by then Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud declined the request in March 2023 and sent him instead to the Punjab and Haryana High Court. In May 2025, a fresh Collegium resolution recommended his return to Rajasthan. He went on to become the acting Chief Justice, a post Justice Mehta's letter says he has now held "for more than last 10 months." items.title: CBSE OSM row: Supreme Court refuses to direct reopening of re-evaluation portal for class XII answer sheets
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday refused to direct the reopening of the CBSE Class XII examination verification and re-evaluation portal for students with grievances over the evaluation of their answer sheets through the On-Screen Marking (OSM) system. A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana observed the portal had already been opened for all candidates for a specified period and that reopening it could trigger lakhs of fresh claims. "If you don't use the bus, you miss the bus," CJI Kant said. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The Court was hearing a petition challenging the manner in which CBSE introduced the OSM system for evaluation of answer sheets. The plea pointed out that OSM was implemented for the first time in 2026 and that teachers were not provided formal training before its implementation. The plea alleged that the introduction of digital scanning resulted in several irregularities, including certain pages of answer sheets not being scanned, illegible scans and answers or pages not being evaluated. items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday sought responses from the Central government and the National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) on a plea challenging NALSA’s August 4 communication directing the discontinuation of contract renewals for lawyers engaged under the Legal Aid Defence Counsel System (LADCS). items.title: Flash floods an 'act of God', ensuing damage to rented building can't be basis of cheating case: J&K High Court
items.summary: Damage caused a building due to flash floods cannot be blamed on its landlord, observed the Jammu and Kashmir High Court recently while quashing a cheating case filed against the landlord and trustees of a school by a person who had taken over its management [ Ghulam Rasool Rather & Ors. v. UT of J&K ]. The woman who had taken over the management claimed that the school's trustees had failed to disclose structural deficiencies in the school building when it was handed over to her. She, therefore, accused the school's trustees and the building's landlord of cheating her. Justice Sanjay Dhar , however, observed that the primary basis for such an allegation was the damage caused to the building after flash floods that occurred in the area in 2013. Flash floods are an act of God and cannot, by itself, form the basis of a criminal cheating case, the Court held. "Merely because water of flash floods entered the school building and it caused damage to the school building does not make out a case of cheating of the petitioners (school trustees, landlord of building). items.title: Court fee in joint writ petitions payable 'per petitioner' if cause of action is individual: Bombay HC
items.summary: The Bombay High Court on Tuesday held that court fees for joint writ petitions filed under Articles 226 or 227 of the Constitution must be paid 'per petitioner' when individual causes of action are espoused [Satyam Surana v. Bombay High Court]. Justice Sandeep V Marne clarified that a single set of court fee suffices only when co-petitioners share a common or identical cause of action. “This facility of convenience made available to the litigants cannot be misused for avoiding payment of court fees,” the Court observed, Justice Sandeep Marne The clarification came after advocate Satyam Surana filed an application seeking a declaration that court fees under the Maharashtra Court Fees Act, 1959 must be levied 'per petition' rather than 'per petitioner'. Surana contended that the statute prescribes a fixed fee for an application or petition presented before the High Court and intentionally omits the phrase 'per petitioner'. He argued that demanding separate fees for each petitioner causes unnecessary financial loss to litigants. items.title: Agencies must unite to trace, deport foreign nationals with fake Aadhaar: Bombay High Court
items.summary: All government agencies must work together to detect and deport foreign nationals using fake or fraudulent Aadhaar cards, the Bombay High Court recently observed [State of Maharashtra v. Unique Identification Authority of India & Ors]. In two separate orders passed on July 27 and August 10, a division bench of Justices AS Gadkari and Kamal Khata emphasised the need for joint action. Justice AS Gadkari and Justice Kamal Khata The bench flagged a concerning pattern where foreign nationals have illegally infiltrated into India and fraudulently obtained basic documents. “Foreign nationals have illegally infiltrated India’s border and have fraudulently obtained basic documents to conceal their true identity and subsequently procured Aadhaar Cards to claim Indian identity. In a few cases, the investigating agencies have reported that such persons have engaged in alleged anti-national activities after securing these fraudulent documents, particularly leveraging the Aadhaar Card to claim false legitimacy as Indian citizens,” the July 27 order noted. items.title: Calcutta High Court stays arrest warrant against TMC MP Mahua Moitra
items.summary: The Calcutta High Court on Tuesday stayed an arrest warrant issued against Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra by a trial court in a case of alleged hate speech [Mahua Moitra v State of West Bengal and Others] A Bench of Justice Debangsu Basak and Justice Aryak Dutt passed the order on Moitra’s petition seeking quashing of the complaint case filed against her before a Krishnanagar court “Till September 30, 2026 or until further orders, police will not execute warrant of arrest issued as against the petitioner on August 19, 2026,” the Court directed. A Krishnanagar court had issued an arrest warrant against Moitra on August 19 after she failed to appear before it. Today, the High Court said that the issue with regard to the jurisdiction of the court which directed issuance of arrest warrant against her requires consideration. Moitra’s counsel earlier submitted that due to a resolution of the local bar association, she could not participate in the complaint case on June 18. It was also argued that the complaint case was pending before a court lacking jurisdiction to hear it. items.title: Ajeet Bharti moves Delhi court for anticipatory bail, says no case made out under SC/ST Act
items.summary: YouTuber and commentator Ajeet Bharti has approached Delhi's Patiala House Court seeking anticipatory bail in the case registered against him under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act (SC/ST Act). The case was heard today by Additional Sessions Judge (ASJ) Saurabh Pratap Singh Laler . Advocate Jai Anant Dehadrai and Pratyush Prasanna appeared for Bharti and argued that no offence under the SC/ST Act was made out against him on the facts of this case. Dehadrai added that the police was yet to issue a notice under Section 35(3) of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) to Bharti. Section 35(3) mandates that police officers must issue a written notice of appearance to an accused person in cases where an immediate arrest is not required. After hearing the case briefly, the Court said that if the police issues a notice to Bharti, the same must be placed before the Court for examination.
